text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
French physicist ANDRE AMPERE was born on this day in 1775. His work with magnetism and electricity led to the "ampere" being used as a measure of intensity of electric current.
English poet LORD BYRON (George Gordon, the 6th Lord Byron), known for his scandalous private life, was born in 1788.
The playwright AUGUST STRINDBERG, dubbed "the Shakespeare of Sweden", was born in 1849.
The British founder member of the Fabian Society, BEATRICE WEBB, was born on this day in 1858.
Australian aviator HARRY HAWKER was born in 1889. He was a test-pilot for SOPWITH, and was the first person to drive a sports car over 100 mph (160 kph).
World famous violinist YEHUDI MENUHIN was born in 1916.
Australian bookmaker and turf identity BILL WATERHOUSE was born in 1922.
The British actor who starred in "THE ELEPHANT MAN", JOHN HURT, was born on this day in 1940.

Australian singer/songwriter with 'INXS' MICHAEL HUTCHENCE was born in 1960. They formed in 1979 and released their first record in May 1980. Hits included "What You Need" (1986), "Need You Tonight" (1987), "Devil Inside" (1988), "New Sensation" (1988) and "Never Tear Us Apart" (1988).
** EVENTS **
1666 : SHAH JAHAN, the Mogul Emperor of India who built
the TAJ MAHAL as a tomb for his beloved wife, died at the age of 74 in the fort where his son imprisoned him 8 years earlier.
1840 : The first British colonists arrived at Port
Nicholson, New Zealand.
1879 : In The Zulu War, 830 British troops were massacred
at ISANDLWANA.
1901 : QUEEN VICTORIA died at Osborne House on the Isle
of Wight at the age of 81, after a 64 year reign.
1905 : At least 500 people were killed or wounded when
Cossack troops fired into a crowd of demonstrators at the Winter Palace in St Petersburg. The massacre became known as "RED SUNDAY".
1924 : RAMSAY MacDONALD became Britain's first Labour
Prime Minister.
1941 : The British captured TOBRUK from German forces.
1944 : The Allies landed at Anzio, Italy, in an operation
codenamed Shingle.
1949 : Chinese leader MAO TSE-TUNG marched into Peking
(Beijing) at the head of his army, to take communist control of the country.
1970 : The Abortion Inquiry in Melbourne was told that

the Chief of the Victorian Homicide Squad, Inspector JACK FORD, was paid $600 a month for almost eight years to protect abortionists. The inquiry heard evidence of payouts totalling thousands of dollars to police. The inspector and three former police officers stood trial following the inquiry.
1972 : The UK, Irish Republic and Denmark joined the
European Economic Community.
1973 : The 36th President of the United States, LYNDON
BAINES JOHNSON, died.
1983 : Swedish tennis star BJORN BORG retired from the
professional circuit at the age of 26, with 6 French Opens and 5 consecutive Wimbledon titles to his name.
1994 : In the US LORENA BOBBITT was found not guilty of
attempted murder, by virtue of temporary insanity. She cut off her husband's penis and threw it on the roadside.
